 Company offers to resurrect the Cybertruck after Tesla ends production
 Chron Follow Abigail Rosenthal Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:01 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:01 PM UTC Tesla won't produce the Cybertruck starting sometime next year. One company is offering to keep it alive. (VCG via Getty Images) Tesla may be halting production of the Cybertruck , but one company wants to see it live on and is offering to take over the remaining fleet. Aftermarket parts and upgrade company Unplugged Performance is pitching Tesla to let them take over the Cybertruck line and even produce a three-row, SUV-style Cybertruck.
 Tesla announced last week that it would stop production of the oft-maligned Cybertruck at Austin's Gigafactory sometime next year to focus on the Cybercab, Tesla's autonomous taxi vehicle.
 In a post on X, Unplugged Performance laid out its deal: Investors would cover the cost, Cybercab would still take priority for battery cells, and Tesla could profit off of a licensing fee, the company's Full Self-Driving mode, and Robotaxi capabilities.
 An open offer to Tesla: We fully support putting Cybercab first, and we'd be glad to take the Cybertruck line off your hands. We'd fund it with a consortium of investors and run it at no cost to Tesla's floor space, headcount, or focus. All of that goes to Cybercab. Cybercab gets first call on battery cells too. We'll wait our turn. Tesla gains incremental profit: a license fee, plus FSD and Robotaxi network revenues on every vehicle built. We'd build the Cybertruck, a three-row CyberSUV, and an unmanned CyberCargo hauler. More autonomous miles, across every surface of this planet and beyond. Worth a conversation?
 - UP (@UnpluggedTesla) November 10, 2026 
 Tesla nor its founder and CEO, Elon Musk, had responded to Unplugged as of publishing time.
 Advertisement Advertisement However, visible replies to Unplugged's pitch were overwhelmingly positive, with some sharing photos of their Cybertrucks and others hankering for imminent upgrades.
 "Are you guys serious? Please say you're serious. I need the truck and SUV," one person replied on X.
 Unplugged Performance also reassured another that the idea was profitable.
 "Our plan is two channels: units deployed to the Robotaxi network for maximum profit per unit, and private sales at a lower profit per unit," Unplugged posted on X. "Both sustainable, both joy-maximizing."
 The Cybertruck has been awash in controversy and problems since its inception. It was first announced in 2019, but production didn't begin until late 2023. Owners reported rusting and that the truck couldn't handle off-roading as it was advertised. Firefighters had to receive special instructions for putting out Cybertruck battery fires. The vehicle also experienced several recalls.
